nodes.summary: With sampling variance `s² = 1 / N`, `r²_g = N h² / (N h² + M)`.
nodes.title: Daetwyler–Dudbridge formula

nodes.summary: Polygenic-score accuracy as a ratio of expectations: `r²_g = h² / (h² + M s²)`. (If `h² = 0` both sides are `0`.)
nodes.title: Polygenic-score accuracy

nodes.summary: With orthogonal standardized training columns, `β̂ = Xᵀ y / N` and residual variance `1 - h²`, `r²_g = N h² / (N h² + M (1 - h²))`. The cited `N h² / (N h² + M)` takes the residual variance to be `1`.
nodes.title: Polygenic-score accuracy in the LD-score model

nodes.summary: The squared correlation of the genetic value and the polygenic score as a ratio of expectations, `𝔼[βᵀβ̂]² / (𝔼[βᵀβ] 𝔼[β̂ᵀβ̂])`: by `integral_score_mul_score`, `βᵀβ̂`, `βᵀβ` and `β̂ᵀβ̂` are the covariance and variances of `xᵀβ` and `xᵀβ̂` over a target population of standardized uncorrelated markers. It is not the expectation of a squared correlation.
nodes.title: Squared accuracy of a polygenic score

nodes.summary: The pooled frequency `p = ∑ i n_i / (2 N)` of the counted allele.
nodes.title: Pooled allele frequency

nodes.summary: The allelic test equals the trend test iff the pooled sample is in Hardy–Weinberg proportions (`n₁² = 4 n₀ n₂`; Sasieni 1997), whenever the trend numerator is nonzero.
nodes.title: The allelic test equals the trend test iff the pooled sample is in Hardy–Weinberg proportions

nodes.summary: Allelic versus trend test (Sasieni 1997): with cases and controls present, a pooled allele frequency strictly between `0` and `1` and a positive score variance, `allelic · 2 p q = trend · Var`.
nodes.title: Allelic versus trend test

nodes.summary: The allelic test: Pearson's statistic of the `2 × 2` table of case and control allele counts (`2N` alleles).
nodes.title: Allelic test statistic

nodes.summary: The `N`-normalized score `β̂ j = X_jᵀ y / N`.
nodes.title: Normalized score in the stratified LD-score model

nodes.summary: The estimated effects `β̂ = β + e`.
nodes.title: Estimated marker effects

nodes.summary: The association statistic `χ² j = N β̂ j ²`.
nodes.title: Association statistic in the stratified LD-score model

nodes.summary: For markers uncorrelated in the sample (`XᵀX` diagonal) without zero columns, the joint estimate is the vector of marginal estimates.
nodes.title: Joint estimate equals marginal estimates for uncorrelated markers

nodes.summary: COJO joint estimate (Yang et al. 2012, eq. (5)): the joint least-squares estimate `(XᵀX)⁻¹ Xᵀ y` equals `(XᵀX)⁻¹ D β̂` in terms of the marginal estimates `β̂`, so it can be computed from summary statistics and `XᵀX`. (Stated for every `X`; it is the least-squares estimate when `XᵀX` is invertible.)
nodes.title: COJO joint estimate

nodes.summary: Unconditionally, the conditional formula equals the nonsingular-inverse formula applied to the algebraic residual `y - X₁ ((X₁ᵀX₁)⁻¹ X₁ᵀ y)`. If both Gram determinants are units, these are the successive least-squares fits on blocks 1 and 2. With a singular Gram matrix they need not minimize residual error. This is in general not the block-2 part of the joint formula on both blocks (the formulas agree when…
nodes.title: Conditional estimate as a fit to the first-block residual

nodes.summary: COJO conditional algebraic formula from summary statistics (Yang et al. 2012, eq. (17)): `b̂₂|b̂₁ = (X₂ᵀX₂)⁻¹ D₂ β̂₂ - (X₂ᵀX₂)⁻¹ X₂ᵀX₁ (X₁ᵀX₁)⁻¹ D₁ β̂₁`.
nodes.title: COJO conditional algebraic formula from summary statistics

nodes.summary: The unconditional algebraic formula from Yang et al. 2012, eq. (15): `(X₂ᵀX₂)⁻¹ X₂ᵀ y - (X₂ᵀX₂)⁻¹ X₂ᵀX₁ (X₁ᵀX₁)⁻¹ X₁ᵀ y`. When both Gram determinants are units, this has the usual interpretation as the block-2 fit conditional on the block-1 fit. For a singular Gram matrix, Mathlib's nonsingular inverse is zero and the value can be a junk value.
nodes.title: Conditional estimate of second-block effects (COJO)

nodes.summary: The squared sample correlation of case status (`1` for cases, `0` for controls) and the genotype score over the `N` individuals of the table.
nodes.title: Squared correlation of case status and genotype score

nodes.summary: The bivariate LD-score model (Bulik-Sullivan et al. 2015b), at the level of the cross second moments that enter `𝔼[z₁ z₂]`: a pool of `n` genotyped individuals with genotype matrix `X`, two GWAS samples `S₁`, `S₂` of the pool (possibly overlapping), effects `β₁`, `β₂` with `∫ β₁ k β₂ l = (ρ_g / M) [k = l]` (genetic covariance `ρ_g`), noises `ε₁`, `ε₂` with `∫ ε₁ i ε₂ i' = ρ_e [i = i']` (residual cross-moment `ρ_e`…
nodes.title: Bivariate LD-score model

nodes.summary: The diagonal `D = diag(XᵀX)` of the Gram matrix.
nodes.title: Diagonal of the genotype Gram matrix

nodes.summary: The model forces `h² ≥ 0` when there is at least one marker.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of heritability in the effect-estimate model

nodes.summary: The training genotype matrix has orthogonal columns with sum of squares `N`, `∑ i, X i k * X i l = N [k = l]`; for centered columns this says that the markers are uncorrelated, with unit sample variance, in the training sample.
nodes.title: Training genotype matrix with orthogonal standardized columns

nodes.summary: `𝔼[β̂ᵀβ̂] = h² + M s²` (for at least one marker).
nodes.title: Expected squared norm of the estimated effects

nodes.summary: `𝔼[βᵀβ̂] = h²` (for at least one marker).
nodes.title: Expected cross product of true and estimated effects

nodes.summary: `𝔼[βᵀβ] = h²` (for at least one marker).
nodes.title: Expected squared norm of the true effects

nodes.summary: Stratified LD-score regression (Finucane et al. 2015): for a standardized genotype matrix and `N ≠ 0`, `𝔼[χ² j] = N ∑_c τ_c ℓ(j, cat c) + σ²_e`. Full-matrix standardization makes every normalized cross product in `stratLDScore` a sample correlation.
nodes.title: Stratified LD-score regression

nodes.summary: One causal variant (the LD-proxy noncentrality; Pritchard & Przeworski 2001): if the genotype matrix is standardized and the only category is the single causal marker `c` with variance `τ`, then for a marker `m` and `N ≠ 0`, `𝔼[χ² m] = N τ r m c ² + σ²_e`.
nodes.title: One causal variant

nodes.summary: The exact expectation of the association statistic in the stratified model, for any genotype matrix: `𝔼[χ² j] = N ∑_c τ_c ℓ(j, cat c) + σ²_e (∑ i, X i j ²) / N`.
nodes.title: Expected association statistic in the stratified LD-score model

nodes.summary: In a target population whose marker genotypes `x j` have raw second moments `∫ x j * x k = [j = k]` (standardized, uncorrelated markers), the scores `xᵀ a` and `xᵀ b` of two effect vectors have raw cross moment `aᵀ b`. With mean-zero genotypes and a probability measure this is the covariance of the genetic value `xᵀ β` and the polygenic score `xᵀ β̂`.
nodes.title: Cross moment of two polygenic scores

nodes.summary: If the two samples have the same normalized cross products with marker `j` and the overlap marker is standardized at `j` (`∑_{i ∈ S₁ ∩ S₂} X i j ² = N_s`), then `𝔼[z₁ j z₂ j] = √(N₁ N₂) ρ_g ℓ_j / M + ρ_e N_s / √(N₁ N₂)`. Here `ρ_e` is only the residual cross-moment specified by `CrossTraitModel`; this theorem does not state the Bulik-Sullivan phenotypic-correlation overlap formula or establish z-score normalization.
nodes.title: Equal normalized-cross-product specialization of the residual cross-moment identity

nodes.summary: With `N₁ = |S₁|`, `N₂ = |S₂|`, `𝔼[z₁ j z₂ j] = √(N₁ N₂) (ρ_g / M) ∑_k r¹ j k r² j k + ρ_e (∑_{i ∈ S₁ ∩ S₂} X i j ²) / √(N₁ N₂)`, with the in-sample normalized cross products `r¹`, `r²` (`sampleCorr`).
nodes.title: Cross-trait scaled-score identity, exact form

nodes.summary: The marginal least-squares estimate `x_jᵀ y / x_jᵀ x_j` of marker `j` (single-marker regression without intercept, on centered genotypes and phenotype as in Yang et al. 2012).
nodes.title: Marginal least-squares estimate of a marker effect

nodes.summary: The trend numerator `U = ∑ i, i (r i S - s i R)` with `R = ∑ r`, `S = ∑ s`.
nodes.title: Numerator of the Cochran–Armitage trend statistic

nodes.summary: The estimates of `ofLDScore` are the normalized scores `Xᵀ y / N` of the LD-score model.
nodes.title: Estimates of the derived model are normalized scores

nodes.summary: The effect-estimate model obtained from the LD-score model when the effects are estimated by the normalized scores `β̂ = Xᵀ y / N` on a training matrix with orthogonal standardized columns: the error is `e k = ∑ i, X i k ε i / N` and its sampling variance is `(1 - h²) / N`.
nodes.title: Effect-estimate model derived from the LD-score model

nodes.summary: Pearson's statistic `n (a d - b c)² / ((a + b)(c + d)(a + c)(b + d))` of a `2 × 2` table `[[a, b], [c, d]]` with `n = a + b + c + d`.
nodes.title: Pearson's chi-squared statistic of a 2 × 2 table

nodes.summary: The phenotype `y = X β + ε`.
nodes.title: Phenotype in the stratified LD-score model

nodes.summary: The effect-estimate model behind polygenic-score accuracy (Daetwyler et al. 2008; Dudbridge 2013), at the level of raw second moments, for `M` independent markers: true effects `beta k` with `∫ β k β l = (h² / M) [k = l]`, estimation errors `err k` with `∫ e k e l = s² [k = l]`, orthogonal to the effects. The estimates are `β̂ = β + e` (`betaHat`). For a probability measure and mean-zero effects and errors these…
nodes.title: Effect-estimate model for polygenic score accuracy

nodes.summary: The model forces `s² ≥ 0` when there is at least one marker.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the sampling error variance of effect estimates

nodes.summary: The in-sample normalized cross product `∑_{i ∈ S} X i j X i k / |S|` of markers `j`, `k` in the sample `S` of a pool of individuals (the sample LD correlation for a matrix standardized within `S`).
nodes.title: In-sample LD correlation

nodes.summary: The observed score variance minus the Hardy–Weinberg score variance `2 p q`: `Var - 2 p (1 - p) = (4 n₀ n₂ - n₁²) / (2 N²)`.
nodes.title: Departure of the genotype-score variance from Hardy–Weinberg

nodes.summary: The pooled genotype-score variance `∑ i² n_i / N - (∑ i n_i / N)²`, `n_i = r i + s i`.
nodes.title: Pooled genotype-score variance

nodes.summary: The stratified normalized-cross-product score `ℓ(j, C) = ∑_{k ∈ C} (X_jᵀ X_k / N)²`. For a standardized genotype matrix this is the stratified LD score of marker `j` with respect to annotation category `C` (Finucane et al. 2015).
nodes.title: Stratified LD score

nodes.summary: The stratified LD-score model (Finucane et al. 2015), at the level of raw second moments: annotation categories `cat c ⊆ {markers}` (possibly overlapping), per-category contributions `tau c`, effects with `∫ β k β l = [k = l] ∑_c τ_c [k ∈ cat c]`, noise with `∫ ε i ε i' = σ²_e [i = i']`, effects orthogonal to noise. The cited model normalizes the phenotypic variance so that `σ²_e ≈ 1`; the confounding term `N a` is…
nodes.title: Stratified LD-score model

nodes.summary: The number of individuals `N = ∑ (r i + s i)`.
nodes.title: Number of individuals in a case-control genotype table

nodes.summary: `Xᵀ y = D β̂` for the marginal estimates `β̂` (Yang et al. 2012). This holds for every genotype matrix: a column with `x_jᵀ x_j = 0` is zero, so both sides vanish there.
nodes.title: Genotype-phenotype cross products from marginal estimates

nodes.summary: The trend test is `N r²` (Armitage 1955): the Cochran–Armitage statistic is `N` times the squared sample correlation of case status and genotype score. (In degenerate tables, where a denominator vanishes, both sides are `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.)
nodes.title: The trend test is `N r²`

nodes.summary: The Cochran–Armitage trend statistic with scores `0, 1, 2` (Armitage 1955): `N U² / (R S (N ∑ i² n_i - (∑ i n_i)²))`.
nodes.title: Cochran–Armitage trend statistic

nodes.summary: The scaled marginal score `z₁ j = √N₁ X_jᵀ y₁ / N₁` of marker `j` for trait 1, computed on `S₁` with `y₁ = X β₁ + ε₁`. The model does not assert the normalization needed for a z-score.
nodes.title: Scaled marginal score for the first trait

nodes.summary: The analogous scaled marginal score `z₂ j` of marker `j` for trait 2, computed on `S₂`.
nodes.title: Scaled marginal score for the second trait

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
